methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: Guest column explicitly frames Virginia's AI challenge as small-business adoption gap rather than infrastructure, signaling awareness that current trajectory concentrates capability in data center hubs while Main Street remains unengaged—a classic shallow concentration pattern.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: $50M AI data center investment adding 200 jobs in Henrico deepens Richmond's emerging tech hub status, but infrastructure investment alone doesn't guarantee distributed capability—signals metro concentration unless workforce development spreads beyond the immediate footprint.

signals.title: University of Virginia Students Help Businesses Explore AI - GovTech
signals.signal_reading: UVA students helping businesses explore AI represents peer-to-peer knowledge transfer and hands-on capability building—a potential distribution mechanism that could spread deep fluency beyond metro hubs if scaled to underserved regions.

signals.title: How one Virginia county’s AI platform protects sensitive data - Route Fifty
signals.signal_reading: Virginia county developing its own AI platform with data privacy protections demonstrates local government building internal capability rather than pure vendor dependence—signals potential for distributed depth if knowledge sharing occurs across jurisdictions.

signals.title: Norfolk looks to add AI dispatcher tool for non-emergency calls - WAVY.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk deploying turnkey AI dispatcher for non-emergency calls exemplifies platform-delivered adoption—broad but shallow implementation that extends AI geographically to Hampton Roads without building local development capacity or deep technical fluency.
